title: Ageing imprecision compounds the effects of fishing selectivity, increasing bias in estimates of growth parameters
content:
Abstract

Accurately estimating fish growth is critical for fisheries management, but growth parameter estimates are often affected by multiple sources of error. While the independent effects of ageing error and fishing selectivity are well documented, their combined effects remain unknown. This study used a simulation approach to determine how ageing imprecision and selectivity (logistic and dome-shaped) compound when estimating growth parameters across four rockfish (Sebastes spp.) life histories. Results demonstrated that ageing imprecision and selectivity exacerbate biases in growth parameter estimates that exceed the error caused by selectivity alone, while selectivity was the primary driver in estimating size-at-age. The magnitude of this compounded bias was heavily dependent on the species' life history and the shape of the selectivity curve. Because growth parameters are frequently used as proxies for critical stock benchmarks like natural mortality and stock depletion, these compounded errors could distort population models. Current growth models fail to account for both sources of error simultaneously, highlighting the critical need to develop integrated frameworks that account for both ageing imprecision and selectivity.
